messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@aws-partner.com>, Joe Patel <joe.patel@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Offer shelving roadmap — revenue pulse + co-sell readiness

Team / Sara,

Quick note to start a short decision thread on which marketplace offers we should actively list across AWS/Azure/GCP versus which we should shelf behind Private Offers or delay. The main idea: reduce operational surface by removing low-velocity SKUs and focus enablement on high-revenue momentum offers that drive co-sell.

Why now:
- Too many skus across clouds adds upkeep (billing mapping, metering, docs).
- Telemetry shows 70% of marketplace MRR comes from ~18% of SKUs in last 90 days.
- Co-sell resources are limited; we should align listing scope with partner GTM capacity.

Proposal (high level):
1) Define "Tier A" SKUs to list in all three clouds (US primary, EU secondary). Criteria: 90-day MRR > $12k AND >50% growth QoQ OR strategic co-sell motions (ISV-led).
2) Define "Tier B" SKUs for single-cloud listing or Private Offer (AWS private offers / Azure marketplace private plan) if they have strong accounts but low global velocity.
3) Turn off or shelf legacy fractional SKUs that require separate metering unless there's an open deal.

Action items I'm asking for this week:
- Marissa: populate the attached matrix with your recommended mapping per cloud + region. Mark any legal/pricing blockers.
- Karthik: confirm constraints around Dedicated SKUs (reserved capacity SKUs) and whether Dedicated-4gpu can be simplified to a single SKU per cloud.
- Kimberly: own the Doc/Marketplace packaging checklist (security artifacts + MSA mapping).
- Sara / Joe: flag any Partner Central / marketplace governance items we must account for (private offers cadence, co-sell registration process).

Attached: marketplace_prio_matrix.csv (starter matrix), co-sell_playbook_v2.pdf (enablement checklist).

Goal: agree on a prioritized shipments list and a 3-week phased rollout plan for US listing canaries by next Friday.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Head of Channel Partnerships
Redwood Inference
---

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@aws-partner.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offer shelving roadmap — revenue pulse + co-sell readiness

Sean — thanks for the clear framing. Quick notes from the AWS side: 

- Private Offers: AWS Private Offers are fine for account-level monetization but expect a ~7 business day SLA for private offer activation if contracts are involved; your legal team needs to attach standard SOW pricing in Partner Central to speed approvals.
- Co-sell registration: For Tier A SKUs we recommend creating co-sell playbook artifacts in Partner Central (win themes, 1-pager, target ICP list). That materially improves AM engagement.
- Metering differences: If you have fractional token-based metering for Hosted plans, GCP marketplace will want a consistent aggregation (per-month usage) vs AWS's per-request mapping — expect minor engineering work to standardize.

I ran a quick pass on the attached matrix (see inline comments). Main ask: can you confirm the canonical SKU names (hosted-small, hosted-large, dedicated-4gpu, private-enterprise)? We want to map to Marketplace product codes on our side.

Happy to join a short sync with Marissa and Karthik to walk the proposed matrix; also can loop in Partner Ops to pre-clear co-sell registration requirements.

Best,

Sara Kim
Partner Solutions Manager — AWS Marketplace
AWS Partner Network

Thanks Sean — I updated the attached CSV with a recommended mapping. High level callouts: 

- Tier A (global): hosted-large, hosted-llm-fast (this is the new verified low-latency offering), dedicated-4gpu. These are the top drivers of MRR and have clear co-sell GTM. Recommend list in AWS+Azure+GCP across US and EU; APAC to be staged later.
- Tier B (cloud-specific or private): hosted-small, burst-pack (short-term burst credits), private-enterprise. Recommend AWS Private Offer for several enterprise customers (Nimbus, CloudBridge pilot) and an Azure private plan for a single EMEA customer requiring local billing.
- Shelf: fractional-credits, legacy-onprem-lite — no open deals and high maintenance. Put a 90-day hold and revisit if an active sales motion appears.

Blocking items:
- Legal needs to confirm if our trial metering terms map cleanly to AWS private offers (Kimberly to chase).
- Engineering: metering standardization work estimate of 2 sprints for GCP mapping.

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) Kimberly: gather security artifacts + partner MSA templates (due Tue 9/7).
2) Karthik: confirm Dedicated SKU simplification decision and owner for capacity mapping by 9/9.
3) Sean/Marissa: sign-off on Tier A list and publish PR to Partner Ops.

I'm attaching the CSV: marketplace_prio_matrix.csv (sheet 1: priority, sheet 2: notes per cloud). I've also added a short playbook checklist in the co-sell_playbook_v2.pdf.

Marissa Cole
Director, Marketplace GTM
Redwood Inference

Strong deck. I approve the phased approach. A couple clarifications before we push to Partner Ops: 

- Canary scope: US-East (AWS) + US-Central (Azure) with hosted-large and dedicated-4gpu only. Confirmed with infra that Dedicated-4gpu capacity can be pooled across regions for the initial rollout (reduces SKU duplication).
- Timeline: week 0 = partner packaging + assets; week 1 = private offer activations for pilot accounts; week 2 = public listing for Tier A in the canary regions; week 3 = expand to EU if canary stability is good.
- Success metrics: 7-day activation rate for private offers, co-sell registration completed for top 10 partner AMs, error rate <1% on metering mapping.

Kimberly: please prepare the security + MSA checklist and upload to the related link (https://redwood.gdrive/reports/DEAL-4982-prio-matrix) by Mon 9/6 so Partner Ops can kick off registrations.

If there are no major objections, Marissa and I will publish the final mapping to Partner Ops and loop Partner Central.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
